purpose: Explain why ontology_only_real ROC-AUC = 0.5013 (chance) on benchmark-v2.
interpretation: Token->SNOMED/RxNorm mapping WORKS (222-446 codes mapped per record); the data integration is real.

The engine's DEFAULT ruleset has only a narrow demographic sex-restriction rule (fires on ~1.5% of gender-flip anomalies) and essentially NO rule that fires on the medication-indication-mismatch (0.11%) or forbidden-cooccurrence/diabetes-type mutual-exclusion (0.00%) families.
Because the anomaly violation rate (0-1.5%) is barely above the normal violation rate (0.10%), there is no ranking signal -> ROC-AUC ~= 0.50.

This is a RULESET-COVERAGE gap, not a benchmark or wiring defect: the scoring rules needed to catch the v2 anomaly RELATIONSHIPS (drug->required indication; type-1 vs type-2 diabetes mutual exclusion; broader sex-restricted concept coverage) are not encoded in the canonical engine's default ruleset.
implication_for_claims: C4 (ontology improves ranking) is NOT supported by benchmark-v2: real-ontology scoring is at chance. C5 (real ontology data integration) remains supported (mapping + coverage are real). Closing the gap = author/curate ontology rules for the v2 anomaly families and re-evaluate; that is a later experiment-phase task, not Phase 3 closure.
note: Reproduce by scoring test.pkl rows {codes, gender, age_group} with the real scorer and bucketing s_ont>0 by anomaly_type.
